# Introduction / Overview

![][image1]

## What are we talking about? 

**THE GUIDING QUESTION: “How should the people of Central Oregon be involved in local and state decisions related to AI technology and infrastructure?”**

This question came through thorough engagement with the Central Oregon community. [Polling and conversations](http://report.bloomproject.us/central-oregon-ai) across Central Oregon in spring 2026 surfaced two priorities: a desire for greater community involvement in decision-making, and AI technology and infrastructure as a topic of particular concern. The Civic Assembly on AI brings the two together. 

Artificial intelligence is a rapidly-developing technology that will likely have far-reaching consequences in our personal lives, the economy, and otherwise. Whether you are optimistic, pessimistic, or unsure about what a future with more AI will bring, many people agree that the people of Central Oregon will be well-served by figuring out how the public can best engage on these issues, before decisions are made that are likely to affect land and other natural resources, the education of Central Oregon’s youth and future workforce, towns, our ability to work and do business, and more.

Through these deliberations, we will to think together about what we want our future to be, what accountability by government to the public means and requires, and what specific steps we can take as voters and taxpayers to ensure Central Oregon’s elected representatives are prepared to shepherd AI-related changes in a direction that can enable the pursuit of life, liberty and happiness for everyone.

—

**Note:** As Civic Assembly delegate, you will arrive with perspectives about AI that may differ from those around you. Some may support new AI data centers; others may oppose them. These are important issues, but the Assembly is *not* designed to settle those particular debates. 

Instead, delegates will consider **how the people of Central Oregon can have a meaningful voice in decisions about AI**, whether those decisions are made by local or state governments, school districts, or other institutions. AI offers one focused, timely topic within the much larger universe of decisions that shape our communities. In the end, delegates will offer a community-centered perspective on how to engage and involve residents when local and state decisions related to AI are made.

How to use these learning materials

In preparation for this Civic Assembly, the Central Oregon Civic Action Project engaged with a wide range of public servants, community-based organizations, community engagement experts, and more. This group pro

The materials are divided into a few key sections: 

- **AI-related Decisions,** laying out the different kinds of decisions that our state and local governments are making related to AI  
- **Public Engagement,** covering how and when the public is able to influence these decisions  
- **Case Studies** on what has worked for other places, and what could still be better

You are not expected to read every word of this document. Instead, we have broken up the materials based on the smaller questions that they can help you answer. Feel free to jump around to the different questions and sections. 

During the Assembly, live presentations and discussions will further support shared understanding. Assembly staff will be able to help find answers to any questions that emerge during the discussions, and local subject-matter experts will also be present to answer more specific questions. 

If you have any questions before then, please add them to the [Question Board](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeccalq6FQQrRKFha2XeWcYJPI8tSGsH-N0KnmmRtyE9NT75A/viewform?usp=publish-editor), where they may also be shared with other delegates to support broader learning. You can also directly email Delegate Concierge Mickie Derting at [mickie@cocap.us](mailto:mickie@cocap.us).
